key_insight: DMW aligns a multimodal vision–language–action driving policy to individual driver preferences by conditioning control decisions on natural-language preference descriptions and learned preference models, producing personalized and interpretable driving behaviors.
problem_solved: Existing end-to-end driving systems optimize for generic objectives or use rigid modes and cannot adapt to individual driving habits or follow natural-language intent; DMW enables per-driver behavioral customization and intent-aware control.
method: Train a vision–language–action policy that ingests onboard sensory input (camera/LiDAR) plus natural-language preference prompts to produce continuous driving actions.

Learn preference alignment via paired demonstrations, preference labels or human feedback: build a preference model / reward estimator and fine-tune the policy to respect stated preferences (contrastive/reward modeling and policy fine-tuning).
Deploy real-time inference and evaluation in simulation and human-in-the-loop tests to validate personalized behaviors, safety trade-offs, and interpretability.
impact: Enables autonomous driving systems that adapt to individual users and accept natural-language instructions, improving user comfort, acceptance, and controllable behavior in safety-critical settings. Practitioners can apply the preference-alignment pattern to other embodied AI systems requiring personalized control.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: vision + language input → preference encoder → action policy (show data flow and conditioning).
Before/after driving traces: same scenario driven by generic policy vs. DMW personalized policy to illustrate behavioral differences (e.g., merge timing, following distance).
Preference embedding visualization (e.g., t-SNE) showing clusters of driver styles and how language prompts map to embeddings.
Evaluation charts: alignment score vs. safety/performance trade-off and user satisfaction ratings from human-in-the-loop studies.
paper_title: Drive My Way: Preference Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model for Personalized Driving
paper_authors: Zehao Wang, Huaide Jiang, Shuaiwu Dong, Yuping Wang, Hang Qiu
